instance: A fatal ±11pp statistic in the paper, a fix-plan that repeated the same error, and a wrong estimand (measuring σ instead of decision-invalidation) all survived until hostile Grok/Codex adversarial review caught them — each catch happened before compute or money was spent, but only because adversarial review was run at all three stages.
check: Run hostile/adversarial review (Grok/Codex) on the paper, then on the fix-plan, then again whenever facts change — before any compute/money spend.

instance: The team was proceeding toward running/publishing a determinism study without having surveyed prior art; a searxng literature survey found Yuan et al. (NeurIPS Oral) already owns the general claim, which would have scooped or gotten the paper rejected a fourth time had it not been caught first.
check: Run a prior-art/literature survey before committing to run or publish a study.

instance: Retrieval-nondeterminism and timeouts were candidate confounds for the observed variance; instead of assuming they mattered, they were actively tested for falsification against data already on disk and ruled out (retrieval was 100% deterministic; timeouts were 1/133) at zero additional cost.
check: Attempt to falsify each candidate confound against existing data before treating it as a live explanation.

instance: A run printed "COMPLETE" but had actually loaded 0 items (a silent-empty run); this was only caught because the run.log was read directly for the "N ingest entries loaded" line instead of trusting the summary status, avoiding a wasted ~10 GPU-hour scale-up.
check: Read the actual run.log for a non-zero "N ingest entries loaded" (and non-empty checkpoint-score.jsonl) before trusting a "COMPLETE" status and scaling up.

instance: The ~$3-6k GPU rental spend was deferred until a free Stage-0/1 run on owned hardware confirmed the effect first, rather than renting compute against an unconfirmed hypothesis.
check: Require a free-stage confirmation of the effect before authorizing any paid compute rental.

instance: Exploring a maximalist $50-200k+team version of the study first was what revealed that the honest first-win was actually $0 on owned hardware, and that the expensive version has diminishing returns — the ceiling had to be priced to make the floor an informed choice rather than a guess.

The paper's fatal flaw: an 11.4% item-level flip-rate (p10+p01) was reported as a ±11pp accuracy-variance band (p10−p01) — two different statistical objects were conflated, and this error survived multiple sessions before being caught.
check: Explicitly define the estimand (what statistic answers the research question) before any measurement is taken or reported.

instance: The v1 determinism fix-plan re-committed the same flip-rate-vs-accuracy conflation it was meant to fix, and also mis-specified the control condition as `workers=1`, which is not actually batch-invariant (batch-invariance requires `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` plus a bit-equality probe).
check: Adversarially review the fix-plan for the same class of error the original bug had, not just for new errors.

instance: Two independent review sessions reaching the same reject conclusion was treated as strong confirming evidence, but both sessions used the same prompts and the same reject objective (correlated, not independent) — the agreement was a hypothesis generator, not confirmation, and this reasoning error was later caught and struck.
check: Before treating multi-reviewer agreement as evidence, confirm the reviewers used independent prompts/objectives, not shared ones.

instance: A run used per-run unique run-ids that matched no ingested memory, so it silently loaded 0 items while still exiting/reporting success — the same failure class as the fleet FM-B7 atom-build embed footgun (a pipeline exiting 0 having done nothing).
check: Assert non-zero work was actually done (e.g. items loaded > 0) before accepting a run as valid, rather than trusting exit code alone.

instance: The `workers=8 vs workers=1` experimental contrast confounded load/throughput/KV-cache pressure with batch composition, so it could not cleanly isolate batch-invariance as the causal variable.
check: Isolate the single variable under test (e.g. via frozen-prompt + forced co-batching / a bit-equality probe) rather than varying a proxy setting that changes multiple things at once.

instance: A k=6 flip experiment was launched without estimating wall-clock time first; its serial (`workers=1`) cells ran ~5h/round (~30h total), a cost discovered only after round 1 had already run — the serial full-eval arm turned out to be ~5x the batched arm's runtime.
check: Estimate total wall-clock time for all experimental arms before committing GPU time, especially for serial/workers=1 configurations.

instance: The locked scorer runs on the same 80B model instance as the generator, coupling scorer and generator such that the noise decomposition cannot admit results until that coupling is broken (frozen generations, re-scored separately).
check: Verify scorer and generator are decoupled (different instances/frozen generations) before trusting a noise decomposition result.

source_anchor: OPERATIONAL FAILURE MODES - silent-empty eval run
instance: The harness exited reporting "COMPLETE" having actually loaded 0 items, due to a wrong run-id or a missing ingest checkpoint.
check: Assert `N ingest entries loaded > 0` and non-empty `checkpoint-score.jsonl` before trusting a run.

instance: Running `pkill -f 'lme-b4 run'` killed the orchestrating shell itself because its own command line contained the matched pattern.
check: Match a unique wrapper name or use recorded PIDs when killing processes, never a substring the killer's own command line shares.

source_anchor: OPERATIONAL FAILURE MODES - feature present but arch-incompatible
instance: The vLLM `batch_invariant` module imports successfully on GB10 but fails at runtime because Triton is not installed/compatible, so the feature appears present but its kernels cannot actually run; fixed by switching to the `vllm-gb10` image (Triton 3.6.0).
check: Verify the feature executes (not just imports) on the target hardware before relying on it.

source_anchor: OPERATIONAL FAILURE MODES - hook false-positive on .env/token path strings
instance: A `versions.env` path string appearing inside a gh-api command tripped the protected-path write guard as a false positive, blocking a legitimate command.

source_anchor: OPERATIONAL FAILURE MODES - rm -rf gated in autonomous mode
instance: Destructive `rm -rf <glob>` commands get denied when running unattended/autonomous, blocking cleanup steps that assumed they'd be allowed.
check: Use fresh output directories instead of deleting; resume-skip logic makes deletion unnecessary.

source_anchor: OPERATIONAL FAILURE MODES - nohup watcher doesn't wake agent
instance: A `nohup … &` detached background watcher wrote logs but never notified/woke the agent on completion, so completion went unnoticed.
check: Use Bash `run_in_background: true` (harness-tracked) instead of `nohup … &` for anything that must re-invoke the agent on completion.
